amendments.body: `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs:324-327` defines `molt_failure_poor_condition_threshold` as a threshold on the blended molt-condition score, but `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:623-638` records `poor_condition_involved` from that blended `condition_factor` while `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs:1396-1401` reports the failure as `condition {raw_condition}<{threshold}` using `min_condition_index`. That can produce impossible diagnostics for reserve-driven failures: a shrimp with healthy raw condition but low reserves can trip `PoorCondition` and emit text like `condition 0.70<0.65`. Either gate `PoorCondition` on raw `condition_index`, or keep the blended-factor test and report the blended factor/reserve shortfall instead of the raw condition index.
amendments.rationale: This is a player-visible correctness bug in the new molt diagnostics. The event log can now contradict the actual modeled inputs, which undermines the acceptance criterion that failures be explainable from surfaced details.

payload.summary: Reviewed the project diff and read the key shrimp/mineral implementation files end-to-end, especially `crates/tank_core/src/systems/shrimp.rs`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/biology.rs`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/events.rs`, `crates/tank_core/src/types/snapshot.rs`, plus the related save/invariant/tracing paths. The core mineral-budget mechanic, parameterization, and regression coverage look solid overall. One live issue remains: molt-failure diagnostics can still misreport reserve-driven failures as low raw condition because the threshold is evaluated on the blended condition factor but rendered against the raw condition index.
